# Agent loops with @solidjs/diagnostics

Solid's dev builds expose two evidence channels — rule diagnostics (stable
codes for known anti-patterns) and attribution (per-re-run causality with
timing and waste accounting). This package captures both into one
serializable artifact. Use it to verify claims about reactive code instead
of inferring them from reading it.

There are five loops. Each takes the same fixture:

```ts
import { captureArtifact } from "@solidjs/diagnostics";

const { artifact } = await captureArtifact(
  () => {
    // mount a tree or exercise a store, then perform the interaction
    // under test; flush() happens automatically at the end
  },
  { scenario: "todo-toggle" }
);
```

## Loop 1 — Generation (write code until the channel is quiet)

After generating or porting a component, run its scenario and read
`artifact.diagnostics`. Every event has a stable `code`; the
`reactivity-diagnostics` skill shipped in `solid-js` maps each code to its
repair. Fix, re-capture, repeat until zero events. Do not allowlist a code
you have not understood — each one is a real defect or a real cost.

```ts
import { expectNoDiagnostics } from "@solidjs/diagnostics";
expectNoDiagnostics(artifact); // throws with the offending events as evidence
```

## Loop 2 — Acceptance (scenario + budget = definition of done)

A component is done when a named scenario stays within an explicit budget.
Budgets are machine-checkable, so "the port is granular" stops being a
judgment call:

```ts
import { assertBudget } from "@solidjs/diagnostics";

assertBudget(artifact, {
  allow: [], // tolerated diagnostic codes
  maxReruns: 2, // total re-run cardinality for the scenario
  maxWastedRuns: 0, // unchanged recomputes (plain, non-held)
  scopes: { TodoRow: 1 }, // per-scope caps; "/regex/" keys also work
  maxSilentHoldMs: 0 // every hold the interaction caused was acknowledged on screen
});
```

Budgets belong in a checked-in JSON file (see `parseBudgetFile`) so CI owns
them and a regression is a test failure, not a review comment. In Vitest,
import the matchers for inline use:

```ts
import "@solidjs/diagnostics/vitest";

expect(artifact).toHaveNoDiagnostics();
expect(artifact).toStayWithinRerunBudget(2, { scope: /TodoRow/ });
expect(artifact).toHaveNoWaste();
```

## Loop 3 — Attribution (why did this run → targeted refactor)

When a budget fails or something feels slow, do not guess — read the
causality:

- `artifact.attribution.reruns[]` — each re-run: `nodeName`, `causes`
  (change chain back to the root write), `selfMs`, `changed`, `phase`.
  A run with `changed: false` and `phase: "plain"` was pure waste.
- `artifact.attribution.costs.scopes` — scopes ranked by self-time with
  `wastedMs`; `costs.writes` — root writes ranked by downstream cost.

Start from the top of the cost tables. The usual repairs: a missing memo
boundary (waste), an unstable memo output (fan-out amplifier), a wide read
that should be split, or a hot value that should be inverted into a store
used as a map keyed by id. Re-capture after each change and diff the rerun counts — the
artifact is the before/after evidence.

## Loop 4 — Responsiveness (the click did something, visibly)

Solid holds a write that lands on async work until the data settles, so the
screen never tears. That is correct — and from the user's side the click did
nothing until the data came back unless something on screen acknowledged the
wait. Agents systematically skip the affordances that do this (`isPending`,
`latest`, `createOptimistic`); this loop makes the omission a test failure.

Set `maxSilentHoldMs: 0` on every scenario that is a user interaction, or
assert directly:

```ts
import { expectNoSilentHolds } from "@solidjs/diagnostics";
expectNoSilentHolds(artifact); // fails with the hold: interaction, held write, blocker, duration
```

When it fails, read `artifact.attribution.feedback.sources` first — the
ranked table of what users waited on: per async source, how many holds, how
many silent, `acknowledgedBy` (which affordance answered, in how many holds),
and which interactions were held. A source acknowledged in some holds and
silent in others means the affordance exists on one screen and is missing on
another; add it where the silent holds happen. Then repair by shape, in this
order:

1. **Show the wait** — read `isPending(() => blocker())` (the blocker is
   named in the failure) in the affected UI and render a busy state.
2. **Reveal the input** — `latest(heldSource)` shows the new value of the
   held write (page number, filter, query) immediately while data catches up.
3. **Predict the outcome** — `createOptimistic`/`createOptimisticStore`
   written alongside the real write (or inside the action) shows the expected
   result now and reverts on failure. For actions this is the primary repair.

Anti-repair: never make the assertion pass by moving the write off the async
path, wrapping it in `untrack`, or splitting the read so the write "commits
faster". That trades a hold for a torn screen and is the bug the hold exists
to prevent. `expectHoldBudget(artifact, ms)` is the separate latency gate —
acknowledged or not, no hold may outlast it — for mocked sources that should
settle within a known time.

`artifact.attribution.feedback.interactions` is the INP-shaped view: per user
event, the synchronous re-run work one dispatch caused (`worstDispatchMs` —
fix through Loop 3) beside the time its writes spent held (`worstHoldMs`,
`silentMs` — fix here). In browser captures the interaction is stamped by the
web runtime; in-process, wrap the write in
`OBSERVE.attribution.withInteraction({ type, target }, () => …)` so holds are
measured from the event and keyed by it. A router that wraps its location
write in `OBSERVE.attribution.withOrigin({ kind: "navigation", name, to, from, params }, () => …)`
names holds by route as well — `SILENT_HOLD` then reads "click on a.nav
(navigation to /users/:id) wrote …", and `feedback.navigations` /
`attribution.history("navigation")` give the per-route view. A redirect declared
with `redirect: n` folds onto the pending navigation (one record, timed from
the click, the abandoned destination in `redirects`) rather than superseding it.

The remaining fact tables in `feedback` have no verdict of their own; read
them when a scenario is slow without being silent:

- `flights` — per async source, `flights`/`landed`/`abandoned`. A source that
  abandons most of its flights re-asks on every input change (search as you
  type); put a debounced or equality-gated derivation between the input and
  the fetch. `long`/`longMs` on a `sources` row is the sibling fact: the
  hold's tail (last input → commit) ran past the long-hold threshold,
  acknowledged or not — the `LONG_HOLD` shape. A spinner over stale content
  is not the answer at that length: key a `Loading` boundary with `on` so the
  fallback shows, or preload/cache so the wait never gets there.
- `fallbacks` — per loading boundary, `shows`/`shownMs`/`flashes`. A flash
  (under 150ms) is a spinner that appeared and vanished; preload, cache, or
  lift the fetch above the boundary. Do not add artificial delay.

Loop 4's structural siblings live in Loop 2's diagnostics list:
`EFFECT_RELAY_TEAR` (derived state via effect — a reader ran twice for one
write, the first frame inconsistent; make it a memo), `IMMUTABLE_UPDATE_IN_STORE`
(spread-copy store writes — mutate the draft or `reconcile`), and
`UNSTABLE_LIST_IDENTITY` (a list rebuilt for equivalent records — key by a
stable field or `reconcile`). Each names its repair in the message.

--- name: solid-2.0 description: Solid 2.0 primer for coding agents. Use when writing, reviewing or migrating Solid 2.0 code (solid-js 2.x, @solidjs/web). The API differs from Solid 1.x and from React; read this before generating, then check unfamiliar names against node_modules/solid-js/CHEATSHEET.md. --- # Solid 2.0 for agents Solid is not React, and 2.0 is not 1.x. Pattern-matching from either is the dominant bug source. Every name below is a `solid-js` export unless noted; DOM APIs (`render`, `hydrate`, `Portal`, `dynamic`) are in `@solidjs/web`. ## Three rules 1. **Props are read, not destructured; pass values, not accessors.** - Wrong: `function C({ name }) {}` and `` - Right: `function C(props) { return

{props.name}

; }` and `` 2. **`createEffect` takes two functions: compute (tracks), then apply (side effects).** - Wrong: `createEffect(() => { el.title = count(); });` - Right: `createEffect(() => count(), v => { el.title = v; });` 3. **Stores are written through the draft.** - Wrong: `setStore("user", "name", "B")` or `setStore(produce(s => ...))` - Right: `setStore(s => { s.user.name = "B"; });` ## 1.x → 2.0 corrections Nothing in the left column exists in 2.0. | Wrong (1.x) | Right (2.0) | | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `import { createStore } from "solid-js/store"` | `import { createStore } from "solid-js"` | | `import { render } from "solid-js/web"` | `import { render } from "@solidjs/web"` | | `"jsxImportSource": "solid-js"` | `"jsxImportSource": "@solidjs/web"` | | `createEffect(fn)` (one argument) | `createEffect(compute, apply)` | | `onMount(fn)` | `onSettled(() => { setup(); return cleanup; })` | | `createEffect(on(dep, fn))` | `createEffect(() => dep(), v => fn(v))` | | `const [d] = createResource(id, fetchX)` | `const d = createMemo(() => fetchX(id()))` under `` | | `d.loading` / `d.error` | `` or `isPending(() => d())` / `` | | `refetch()` | `refresh(d)` (`affects(d); refresh(d)` to read as pending) | | `` / `` | `` / `` | | `` | ` ...}>` (heals automatically) | | `` | `` | | `batch(fn)` | not needed: updates batch per microtask; `flush()` applies now | | `startTransition` / `useTransition` | built-in transitions: `action(...)`, `isPending`, optimistic APIs | | `createComputed` | `createMemo`, split `createEffect`, or `createSignal(fn)` | | `mergeProps` / `splitProps` / `unwrap` | `merge` / `omit` / `snapshot` | | `produce`, `createMutable`, `modifyMutable` | draft setters are the default in `createStore` | | `createSelector` | `createProjection` (or `createStore(fn)`) | | `` | `` | | `classList={{ a: x() }}` | `class={{ a: x() }}` or `class={["base", { a: x() }]}` | | `use:dir={x}` / `attr:` / `on:` / `tabIndex` | `ref={dir(x)}` / plain attributes / `onClick` / `tabindex` | | `onError` / `catchError` | `` or `createEffect(c, { effect, error })` | | `from(source)` / `observable` | `createMemo(() => from(source))`; push out with `createEffect` | Also: - Reads lag writes: `setX(1); x()` still returns the old value until the microtask or `flush()`. In tests, `flush()` before asserting. - Effects never compare: when the compute re-runs, apply and the previous cleanup run again even if compute returned an equal value. To skip work on an unchanged value, read a memo in the compute: `const active = createMemo(() => status() === "active"); createEffect(() => active(), v => ...)`. The memo's `equals` (default `===`) stops the re-run. - No writes inside a memo, effect compute, or component body (dev throws). Write from event handlers, `onSettled`, or actions. - Writes in one synchronous frame land together: if one starts async work (a navigation, a refetch), the rest are held with it. To land a write on its own (close a menu before calling `props.onSelect`), wrap it in `onFlush(() => setOpen(false))`. Not `queueMicrotask` or `setTimeout`. - Hydration adopts server answers without re-asking, but runs each adopted compute once to track reads with fake `Promise`/`fetch` that never settle. Never store a promise or `import()` created inside a compute in a cache that outlives it; cache resolved values, or start the load outside. - No reactive reads at the top of a component body; read in JSX, a memo, an effect's compute, or hand a hook an accessor (`useThing(() => props.id)`; JSX props still take values). Flow callbacks (``, ``, ``) are owners, not tracking scopes: read their accessor arguments in JSX, not at the top. - Never use `untrack` to silence `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED`: the value still goes stale, and the warning was the only sign. Move the read instead (see that code's section in the diagnostics skill). Hooks and adapters take accessors and read them inside their own memos and effects. - ``: default gives a raw item and an index accessor; `keyed={false}` gives an item accessor and a plain number. ``: `i` is a number. - `onClick={cond() ? a : b}` binds once; decide inside a stable handler. - `on:`, `oncapture:`, `attr:`, `bool:`, `use:` and `classList` on a native element are compile errors; the message names the replacement above. - Inputs aren't strictly controlled: `value={x()}` writes only when the binding re-runs — and a change to any other dynamic attribute in the same template re-runs it (dev warns `UNCOMMITTED_INPUT_OVERWRITTEN` when that erases typed text). Keep typing in a draft signal (`onInput`), commit on `onChange`/submit; when a handler rejects input, also set `e.currentTarget.value = next` (an unchanged signal won't revert the DOM). ## Primitives to reach for | Primitive | Use | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `createSignal(0)` / `createSignal(() => fetchUser(id()))` | plain signal / writable derived value, sync or async; read by calling it | | `createMemo(() => fetchX(id()))` | read-only derived value; a Promise result is pending until it lands | | `createProjection(async () => api.list(), [], { key: "id" })` | read-only derived store with keyed reconciliation | | `createOptimisticStore(() => api.list(), [])` | store whose optimistic writes revert when the transition settles | | `action(function* (x) { write(); yield api.put(x); refresh(d); })` | mutation with transition coordination; optimistic writes go inside

frontmatter.description: Rules for writing Solid 2.0 server components ("use server" functions that return a template) and their slots with @solidjs/web. Use when writing or reviewing a server component, deciding what lives on the server versus the client, or wiring a slot.

skills.excerpt:
--- name: server-components description: Rules for writing Solid 2.0 server components ("use server" functions that return a template) and their slots with @solidjs/web. Use when writing or reviewing a server component, deciding what lives on the server versus the client, or wiring a slot. --- # Writing Solid server components with slots A Solid server component is a `"use server"` function that returns a template; the browser receives its markup and never its code. Anything the client contributes goes through a **slot** on the component's props: a client component the client places at a position in the server's markup. This guide is the set of rules an author — a person or an agent — needs to write one correctly the first time. The design record is `documentation/server-components/server-components-principles.md`; this file is the operative subset. ## Where things go > **An element lives where the data that creates it lives.** - Exists because of **server data** (a todo row, a nav link, a search form the server renders)? It is **server markup**. A mutation on it is a form `action` — it works without JavaScript, and the router marks a submission in flight (`aria-busy`) so CSS can show the intent. - Needs **client behavior or client state** (a handler, an optimistic add, a modal, a drag ghost, an editor open over a field)? It is a **client component** placed through a **slot**. When the client confirms an optimistic entity and the server renders it, the row _becomes_ server markup; `$key` on the element reconciles the two. ## Slots ```tsx import type { Slot } from "@solidjs/web/frames"; interface TodosProps { pending: Slot; // no props editor: Slot<{ id: string; title: string }>; // props from the server } ``` A slot is placed as an element: ``, ``. The client owns the nodes between the slot's markers; the server's markup around them stays the server's. ```tsx export async function todoList() { "use server"; const todos = await db.list(); return (props: TodosProps) => (
    {todos.map(t => (
  • {t.title}
    • ))}
); } ``` The client passes the fill — a component of the slot's props: ```tsx } pending={() => {…}} /> ``` - **The fill runs once per occurrence, as a component body does.** It runs untracked, under the occurrence's owner, with live props. State it creates (a signal, a memo, an `onCleanup`) lives as long as the occurrence. A top-level read is read once, and `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` names it ("the \`editor\` template-slot fill"). - **Place slots as JSX, not calls.** The compiler wraps each prop in a getter so the read defers to the slot border; a call form (`props.status({ … })`) evaluates its args eagerly in the server component's body. - **`$key` is optional.** Add it when the fill holds its own state (an edit draft, a signal created inside) that must follow the entity across refetches and reorders. - **An async value crosses with `asyncArg`.** `` ships the promise or async iterable; the fill's read settles (suspends until the first value). ## Behavior on server markup A handler on a server-rendered element cannot come from the server: a server function never runs in the browser. Pick one: - **A form.** A mutation is `
`; it works before JavaScript and needs no client code. - **A client component that owns the element.** Move the control into a slot's fill (``, rendering the checkbox on the client). - **One delegated listener.** For many identical controls inside server markup (a copy button on every code block), place one slot occurrence whose component registers a single document listener in `onSettled` and finds its target from the event (`closest("button.copy-code")`). Inside a live hole this is the shape that keeps the hole streaming: a slot placed inside a live hole latches it (`SSR_LIVE_HOLE_LATCHED`, `data.cause` `"records"`). `examples/chat`'s Copy button is this shape. ## Shared components One component can render on both sides. Put `$key={props.id}` on the element it renders (morph identity) — the slot's own `$key` is a different key for a different job. Do not read `document`/`window` during render; that is the ordinary isomorphic rule. ## Compiling With `@solidjs/vite-plugin`, `solid({ ssr: true, serverFunctions: { components: true } })` is the turnkey setup (the examples under `examples/todos-server`, `examples/notes`, `examples/chat`).
